fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Road; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Walkway; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access point with reflective address signage visible from the approach road.
• Keep the access road clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the building without obstruction.
• Mark a designated emergency vehicle turnaround or staging area near the main building, as a single access point limits forward movement options.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access road to maintain clear sightlines for approaching emergency vehicles.
• Mark a pedestrian evacuation route from the rear of the building to the nearest accessible point, given limited rear vehicle access.
• Keep walkways clear of obstacles to allow responders to move around the building on foot.
• Identify and mark any gate or fence access points with visible signage to reduce search time for responders arriving from the single entry.
• Post a site map showing building layout, the single access point, and fence openings at or near the main entry for arriving responders.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Building; Large Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Open Paved Area; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Near Access Route; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin the tree cluster nearest to the building to create a gap between the trees and the structure.
• Trim branches from large trees that extend toward or over the building roofline or walls.
• Clear shrubs and ground vegetation growing directly against the building's exterior walls.
• Thin scattered shrubs and ground vegetation along the access route to keep the travel lane clear and visible.
• Trim tree branches that hang over or crowd the sides of the access route.
• Keep the open paved area free of dead leaves, debris, and any vegetation encroachment from surrounding trees and shrubs.
• Maintain the open area between landscaping and the building — do not allow shrubs or ground vegetation to close that gap.
